name: Easy Store Management for WooCommerce
author: Fernando Tellado

sections.description:
Easy Store Management for WooCommerce turns the WordPress admin into a clean, focused store workspace: no posts, no pages, no plugin menus, no dashboard noise. Just orders, products and customers.

Easy Store Mode, on and off in one click

The simplified admin is a mode, not a life sentence. Pick which roles get it by default (Shop manager, out of the box) and everyone can flip it for themselves from a switch in the admin bar or from their user profile. An administrator who wants the calm store view gets it in one click, and gets the full WordPress back the same way.

Key features

  • Clean interface: hides everything that is not store related, menus, dashboard widgets and admin bar items
  • Reorganized menus: Orders and Customers get their own top-level menu, WooCommerce becomes “Store”
  • Order shortcuts: an Orders menu in the admin bar with a counter of orders waiting for payment or on hold, one entry per status, and a search box to jump straight to an order by number or customer email
  • Low stock warning: a heads-up in the admin bar when products drop below your WooCommerce low stock threshold, opening the products list filtered to what is running out
  • Land where you work: log in and go straight to Orders instead of the Dashboard
  • Quick user switching: look at the store through a customer account to reproduce a cart or checkout problem, and come back to your own account in one click
  • Fully configurable: a settings page under WooCommerce where every one of the above can be turned on or off
  • You decide what stays: the menus and the dashboard widgets your site really has are listed on the settings page, so keeping the ones you use is a matter of ticking a box, with no slugs to look up
  • Menus in working order: Store, Orders, Products, Customers, Users, Withdrawals, Analytics and Marketing, with the Payments shortcut out of the way
  • Plays well with your other plugins: the Users screen stays available so User Switching keeps working, the Consent log of Terms & Conditions Consent Log is reachable, and the Withdrawals screen of EU Withdrawal Compliance shows up for whoever has been given permission to handle requests
  • HPOS ready: every order link points at the right screen whether your store uses High-Performance Order Storage or the classic one

About user switching

Site administrators can switch to any user they are allowed to edit, the usual WordPress rule. Anybody else, a shop manager in practice, needs an administrator to turn on the delegation setting first. Even then they can only reach accounts whose roles are all on the switchable list and that hold no administrative capability, so an administrator account is never reachable that way. If you already use the User Switching plugin, this feature steps aside and lets it do the work.

A note on what this plugin is

Hiding menus is about comfort and focus, not about security. What each person is allowed to do is still decided by their WordPress capabilities, exactly as before installing this plugin.

sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/easy-store-management-ayudawp directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Make sure WooCommerce is installed and activated.
  4. Out of the box, users with the “Shop manager” role get Easy Store Mode. Adjust anything you want in WooCommerce → Easy Store Management.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin affect administrators?

Not unless you want it to. By default only the Shop manager role gets Easy Store Mode. Any administrator can turn it on for themselves from the admin bar switch, and turn it off again the same way.

I turned Easy Store Mode on and half my menus are gone. How do I get out?

The Easy Store Mode switch stays in the admin bar the whole time, in both the dashboard and the front end. Click it and you are back to the full WordPress admin. Your own profile also has the setting.

Can I choose what gets hidden?

Yes. The settings page lets you turn each piece on or off, and it lists the top-level menus and the dashboard widgets your site has so you can tick the ones you want to keep. Anything the list cannot show can still be typed by hand: the slug works, and so does the address of the screen. That includes screens that hang off another menu, such as options-general.php?page=whatever, and in that case the menu they hang off comes back carrying only what you asked for.

Why is the Users menu still there?

Because a store needs it. It is what makes the User Switching plugin usable, so you can look at the store through a customer account, and it is where Terms & Conditions Consent Log puts its Consent log screen. Keeping the menu grants nothing: each person still sees and does only what their own role allows. You can hide it from the settings if you would rather not have it.

Is this a way to restrict what shop managers can do?

No, and it is worth being clear about it. This plugin changes what people see, not what they are allowed to do. Permissions are still WordPress capabilities. If you need real restrictions, use a role editor.

Can shop managers switch to another user?

Only if an administrator turns on the delegation setting, and even then only to accounts whose roles are all on the switchable list and that hold no administrative capability. Without that setting, switching is limited to site administrators. It is a deliberate, opt-in decision, and it can be taken back at any time.

Does it work with High-Performance Order Storage?

Yes. Every order link, menu and counter follows whichever order storage your store uses.

Will this work with other WooCommerce extensions?

Yes. The plugin preserves WooCommerce related menus and dashboard widgets from extensions, and third party plugins can declare their own dashboard widgets as store related with the ayudawp_esm_is_woocommerce_widget filter.

What happens if I deactivate WooCommerce?

The plugin shows an admin notice and stops applying any customization.
sections.changelog:
2.1.0

  • New: Pick the menus to keep from a list of the ones your site really has, instead of typing slugs. Every top-level menu Easy Store Mode would hide is on it, with its name and its slug.
  • New: Pick the dashboard widgets to keep the same way. The widgets your active plugins add, the ones “Clean the dashboard” would take out, are listed so you can keep whichever ones you use.
  • New: Screens that hang off another menu can be kept too, which was never possible before. Paste the address of the one you want, options-general.php?page=whatever for instance, and the menu it hangs off comes back carrying only that screen and not everything it had, so asking for one settings page does not hand you back the whole Settings menu.
  • Improved: The box for typing menus by hand now takes the address of the screen too. Paste admin.php?page=whatever, or the whole URL out of the address bar, and it becomes the slug when you save.
  • Improved: Tested with WooCommerce 11.0.
  • Fix: Menus listed to be kept visible stayed hidden when they were written as the address of the screen, which is what the address bar gives you and what the examples in that very setting pointed at. A plugin page is registered under a bare slug, joinchat, and not under admin.php?page=joinchat. Both forms are accepted now, and the examples have been rewritten. Site Kit and Joinchat were the usual casualties.
  • Fix: Media and Pages could not be kept visible at all, the two examples the setting itself suggested. Both were on an internal removal list that ran before the setting was ever read. That list now leaves alone anything you have asked to keep.

For older changelog entries, please check the changelog.txt file
